INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which habit helps you listen well? (1 mark)
   A. Talking to a neighbour
   B. Playing with a pencil
   C. Looking at the floor
   D. Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker

2. Which sentence uses a comma correctly for speaking to someone? (1 mark)
   A. Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   B. Wanjiku please, bring the umbrella
   C. Wanjiku please bring the, umbrella.
   D. Wanjiku please bring, the umbrella.

3. Reading a text once for the general meaning is done (1 mark)
   A. first, before looking at details
   B. last, after everything
   C. only with a partner
   D. never

4. What is a polite way to disagree in a debate? (1 mark)
   A. I respectfully disagree
   B. You are wrong and silly
   C. Leave now
   D. Shut up

5. How should you read a sad poem? (1 mark)
   A. Fast and loudly
   B. Slowly and softly
   C. Without a pause
   D. Laughing

6. What is a resource person? (1 mark)
   A. A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   B. A pupil who is late
   C. A kind of book
   D. A bag for books

7. The goat is inside the shed. Which preposition shows this? (1 mark)
   A. in
   B. outside
   C. between
   D. behind

8. Which is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The red pen.
   B. I bought a pen.
   C. I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   D. A pen

9. Which tense is used to tell a story about what happened? (1 mark)
   A. Only questions
   B. Only the future
   C. No tense
   D. The past tense

10. What is good telephone manner? (1 mark)
   A. Interrupting
   B. Calling very late for no reason
   C. Speaking with food in your mouth
   D. Speaking clearly and giving your name

11. Which sentence should come first when making tea? (1 mark)
   A. Finally, serve the tea.
   B. Then pour the milk.
   C. Next, drink it.
   D. First, boil the water.

12. Which of these is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. The door is red.
   B. Close the door.
   C. The door was open.
   D. A door has a handle.

13. Which is a polite phrase to ask someone to repeat? (1 mark)
   A. Say it again now
   B. Stop talking
   C. Could you repeat that, please?
   D. What did you say?

14. Where should your class keep collected forms? (1 mark)
   A. In the river
   B. In a portfolio
   C. Under a stone
   D. In the fire

15. Which value should be shown in a market skit? (1 mark)
   A. Rudeness
   B. Cheating
   C. Stealing
   D. Honesty, such as giving correct change

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Read: Fire can be dangerous. Never play with matches. Ask an adult to light the stove. If your clothes catch fire, stop, drop and roll. State the main idea and list three details. (5 marks)

17. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)

18. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)

19. Write the plural of each English noun: plate, tomato. (2 marks)

20. What is a verb? Give two examples. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Sitting where you can see and hear the speaker
   You can follow better when you see and hear clearly.

2. A — Wanjiku, please bring the umbrella.
   A comma follows the name of the person addressed.

3. A — first, before looking at details
   A first reading gives the main idea.

4. A — I respectfully disagree
   Polite words show respect.

5. B — Slowly and softly
   Slow and soft matches sadness.

6. A — A person with special knowledge who visits to teach
   A nurse visiting a class is an example of a resource person.

7. A — in
   In shows something is inside.

8. C — I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   It joins two sentences with so.

9. D — The past tense
   Stories about past events use the past.

10. D — Speaking clearly and giving your name
   Clarity and courtesy help.

11. D — First, boil the water.
   Boiling water is the first step.

12. B — Close the door.
   Close the door tells you what to do.

13. C — Could you repeat that, please?
   Please and could show politeness.

14. B — In a portfolio
   A portfolio keeps them organised.

15. D — Honesty, such as giving correct change
   Skits can show good values.

SECTION B
----
16. (5 marks)
   Answer: Main idea: Fire is dangerous and needs care. Details: never play with matches, ask an adult to light the stove, stop drop and roll.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for the main idea and one mark for each of three details.

17. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

19. (2 marks)
   Answer: plates, tomatoes
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

20. (2 marks)
   Answer: A verb is an action word. Examples: run, close, bring, put.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for two correct examples.
